title: The effect of YouTube video platform on the students’ English-speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation in a communicative English Skills II course: First year undergraduate students in focus
content:
by Mesfin Mekuria Dangore, Elias Woemego Bushisso, Kassa Mihiretie Woldeyes

The major aim of this study was to examine the effects of the YouTube video platform on English speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation among first year undergraduate students at Wolaita Sodo University, Ethiopia. A quasi-experimental design involving two intact groups was employed. One group served as the treatment group (N = 52), while the other served as the comparison group (N = 52). To collect the data, pre- and post-intervention English speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation questionnaires were administered to both groups. To contextualize and complement the quantitative findings, qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with six purposively selected students. The students in the treatment group were taught speaking through the YouTube video platform for 16 weeks, whereas the comparison group received conventional English speaking instruction. After confirming that all statistical assumptions were satisfied, the data were analyzed using one-way MANOVA, together with paired samples t-test, but the qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The results revealed that students in the treatment group demonstrated significantly higher levels of English speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation compared to the comparison group. The results suggest that the YouTube video platform is an effective instructional approach for enhancing English as a Foreign Language learners’ English speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation, highlighting its value as a pedagogical tool for English speaking instruction. Thus, English as foreign language teachers are suggested to use YouTube video platform in their instructional strategies.
author: Mesfin Mekuria Dangore
